question: Is SQLite suitable for production web applications?
aliases: Can SQLite be used in production for web apps?
Should I use SQLite for a production web application?

plan.objective: Assess whether SQLite is suitable as the database for production web applications, and under what conditions.
plan.interpretation: Evaluate SQLite for production web applications by looking at write concurrency, operational simplicity, and the situations where a client/server database fits better.
assumptions: "Production web application" means a server-side application serving real users, not a prototype.

criteria.description: SQLite handles the traffic and write concurrency of typical production web applications
Situations where a client/server database fits better

queries.purpose: When to choose a client/server database

steps: Read SQLite's own guidance on appropriate uses
Collect production experience reports, including negative ones
Identify the conditions that decide the answer

documents.title: Appropriate uses for SQLite
documents.snippet: SQLite works great as the database engine for most low to medium traffic websites.
documents.content:
Appropriate uses for SQLite

SQLite works great as the database engine for most low to medium traffic websites.

If many clients need to write to the database at the same instant, a client/server database may be a better choice.

facts.quote: SQLite works great as the database engine for most low to medium traffic websites
facts.claim: SQLite's documentation says it works well as the database engine for most low to medium traffic websites.

facts.quote: If many clients need to write to the database at the same instant, a client/server database may be a better choice
facts.claim: SQLite's documentation says a client/server database may be a better choice when many clients need to write at the same instant.

documents.title: Write-ahead logging
documents.snippet: In WAL mode, readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers.
documents.content:
Write-ahead logging

In WAL mode, readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers, so reading and writing can proceed concurrently.

WAL mode still allows only one writer at a time. Other connections that try to write wait until the current write transaction finishes.

facts.quote: In WAL mode, readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers, so reading and writing can proceed concurrently
facts.claim: In WAL mode, SQLite readers and the writer do not block each other, so reading and writing can proceed concurrently.

facts.quote: WAL mode still allows only one writer at a time
facts.claim: Even in WAL mode, SQLite allows only one writer at a time.

documents.title: Two years of running SQLite in production
documents.snippet: We have served our production web application from SQLite in WAL mode for two years.
documents.content:
Two years of running SQLite in production

We have served our production web application from SQLite in WAL mode for two years without write contention problems.

Backups are a matter of copying one file with the online backup API or streaming it to object storage.

facts.quote: We have served our production web application from SQLite in WAL mode for two years without write contention problems
facts.claim: One team reports serving a production web application from SQLite in WAL mode for two years without write contention problems.

facts.quote: Backups are a matter of copying one file with the online backup API or streaming it to object storage
facts.claim: Backing up SQLite means copying one file with the online backup API or streaming it to object storage.

documents.title: Why we moved off SQLite
documents.snippet: Under bursts of concurrent writes, our web application returned database is locked errors.
documents.content:
Why we moved off SQLite

Under bursts of concurrent writes, our web application returned database is locked errors until we moved to PostgreSQL.

SQLite was not a good fit for our write-heavy production workload.

facts.quote: Under bursts of concurrent writes, our web application returned database is locked errors until we moved to PostgreSQL
facts.claim: Another team reports 'database is locked' errors under bursts of concurrent writes until it moved to PostgreSQL.

facts.quote: SQLite was not a good fit for our write-heavy production workload
facts.claim: That team found SQLite was not a good fit for its write-heavy production workload.

documents.title: SQLite or a client/server database?
documents.snippet: Applications that run on several servers usually need a client/server database.
documents.content:
SQLite or a client/server database?

SQLite needs no separate server process, which removes a component to deploy and monitor.

Applications that run on several servers usually need a client/server database, because SQLite is designed to be accessed from a single machine.

facts.quote: SQLite needs no separate server process, which removes a component to deploy and monitor
facts.claim: SQLite needs no separate server process, which removes a component to deploy and monitor.

facts.quote: Applications that run on several servers usually need a client/server database, because SQLite is designed to be accessed from a single machine
facts.claim: Applications that run on several servers usually need a client/server database, because SQLite is designed for access from a single machine.

documents.title: Reducing 'database is locked' errors in SQLite
documents.snippet: Setting a busy timeout and keeping write transactions short reduces locking errors.
documents.content:
Reducing database is locked errors in SQLite

Setting a busy timeout and keeping write transactions short reduces database is locked errors, but it does not remove the single-writer limit.

Measure your peak write rate before deciding whether that limit matters for your application.

facts.quote: Setting a busy timeout and keeping write transactions short reduces database is locked errors, but it does not remove the single-writer limit
facts.claim: A busy timeout and short write transactions reduce 'database is locked' errors but do not remove SQLite's single-writer limit.

short_answer.text: It depends on the write load. SQLite works well for most low to medium traffic websites, and in WAL mode reading and writing can proceed concurrently, but it still allows only one writer at a time. Sources disagree on whether that limit causes problems in production: one team ran SQLite in WAL mode for two years without write contention problems, while another hit database is locked errors under bursts of concurrent writes. Applications that run on several servers usually need a client/server database.

synthesis.conflict_description: Production reports disagree on write concurrency: one team ran SQLite in WAL mode for two years without contention, while another hit 'database is locked' errors under bursts of concurrent writes.
limitations: The production reports are single-team experiences with different workloads, so they do not establish a general write-rate threshold.
next_steps: Measure your application's peak concurrent write rate and test SQLite in WAL mode with a busy timeout under that load.
Choose a client/server database if the application must run on several servers.
